chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The sons of Al-Mirdas (Al-Abbas) – whoever draws near to them, they make him an unbeliever; and whoever distances himself from them, they impoverish him; and whoever opposes them, they kill him; and whoever fortifies himself against them, they lower him; and whoever flees from them, they catch him, until their government/dynasty ends.

key_terms.أَكْفَرُوهُ: They made him an unbeliever / turned him into a disbeliever
key_terms.وُلْدُ الْمِرْدَاسِ: The sons of Al-Mirdas (a title for Al-Abbas or a ruling class)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the 'sons of Al-Mirdas' and how do they treat different types of people?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Al-Mirdas' (often interpreted as the Umayyads or specifically Al-Abbas ibn Ali) symbolizes the ruling elite whose authority is characterized by pervasive, inescapable control over the populace regardless of one's stance—whether through proximity, distance, opposition, or flight. This hadith highlights the transient nature of their power ('until their state ends'), a theme central to Shia political theology regarding the eventual rise of the Mahdi and the collapse of unjust regimes.
